clue.text: An ounce of white stuff — and fixed parole date!

parts.note: snow is the white stuff that falls in winter

indicators.note: something fixed has been rigged or rearranged, so the letters of parole are reworked

explanation.surface: A prisoner's release date has been rigged, along with an ounce of some white powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' turns PAROLE into LEOPAR, which with D completes the second word. 'Ounce' looks like a weight but is the old name for a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the large pale-coated cat of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Formally greet king — a Spanish worker of miracles

parts.note: to salute someone is to greet them formally
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is greeted ceremonially as a Spanish miracle-worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a rare dictionary sense: a 'saludador', a Spanish folk healer believed to cure by breath or touch, was called by this English name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records this term for a Spanish quack healer, the saludador, credited with miraculous cures.

clue.text: What may follow November's spelling award?

definitions.meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet used for spelling out letters, the word for N is followed by the word for O
the golden statuette given by the Academy for film achievement

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which prize might come after a November spelling bee.
explanation.walkthrough: In the radio spelling alphabet November stands for N, and the code word for the next letter, O, is also the name of the film award.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy's film prize is the statuette, and the same name is the radio code word for the letter after N.

clue.text: Oscillate, but sign note

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone wavers back and forth but then signs a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To librate is to sway or waver slightly, as a balance does before settling.

clue.text: For starters, only chiropractors can identify place under the back of the head

indicators.note: starters are the first parts, so the opening letter of each of the next seven words is taken

explanation.surface: Only a chiropractor can locate a certain spot at the base of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The occiput is the anatomical term for the rear part of the skull.

clue.text: Separated people with time to find accommodation

parts.note: separated people are living apart
men are people

explanation.surface: A separated couple need time to find somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat or set of rooms rented as a home is a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Looked for water around river, then slept

indicators.note: around tells us the dowsing word wraps itself about the river's letter

parts.note: to dowse is to search for underground water with a divining rod

explanation.surface: A water diviner searched round a river, then dozed off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drowse is to doze, so a past-tense form means slept lightly.

clue.text: The young of fowl perhaps eaten by one?

definitions.text: The young of fowl perhaps eaten by one?

indicators.note: of places the parent before its young, so the rearranged letters come first
perhaps suggests the word fowl is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: a cub is the young of a carnivore such as a fox or bear

explanation.surface: A predator's offspring is pictured snacking on poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges FOWL into WOLF; the young of that is a CUB. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a young predator by which a fowl may be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A young wolf, a pup of the pack, would happily dine on a chicken.

clue.text: Mistake on the anaesthetic might generate this call!

parts.note: wrong means mistaken, an error
an anaesthetic numbs, so cryptically it is a numb-er, a thing that numbs

explanation.surface: An error over the anaesthetic might prompt a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece is read as 'numb-er', something that numbs, not the counting word; the whole is a telephone call to the wrong line.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone call that reaches someone other than the person intended is a misdial.

clue.text: Cold leg of pork and egg is just one of 23

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ham is the cured leg of a pig
O looks like an egg, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Cold ham and egg is merely one of the dishes on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is ANIMALS, the theme; this goat-antelope of mountain ranges is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The chamois is a nimble goat-antelope of European mountains, one creature among many.

clue.text: Noise of brakes on slow manoeuvre from 23

parts.note: brakes applied hard make a screech

indicators.note: to manoeuvre the word slow is to move its letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Brakes squeal as a driver performs a slow manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' turns SLOW into OWLS. 23 across is ANIMALS: these birds are among them.
explanation.definitionFit: These small owls, named for their shrill cry, are birds and so creatures of the wild.

clue.text: In London it's more than warm enough for a 23

indicators.note: the Cockney accent of London drops the H at the start of a word

parts.note: something more than warm enough is hotter

explanation.surface: It's a hotter day in the capital than anyone needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop initial H, so 'hotter' becomes 'otter. 23 across is ANIMALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a fish-eating river mammal, one creature of the theme.

clue.text: Tripe cooked with peas as a starter?

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients prepared and changed, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Offal stewed with peas is served as the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges TRIPE and PEAS together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dish served before the main course to whet the appetite is a starter.

clue.text: Blunder, accepting one runs for a 23!

indicators.note: accepting means the blunder word takes in the other letters

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone admits making a blunder by accepting one who runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is ANIMALS: this long-necked African grazer is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is the tall long-necked African mammal, one creature of the theme.

clue.text: Way of working with wire on one clock

parts.note: flex is electrical cable or wire
I is the Roman numeral for one
to clock something is to time it

explanation.surface: An electrician fits a wire to a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A system that lets staff choose their own start and finish hours is a work arrangement.

clue.text: A dull coat in olive, for example, for a sewer's help

indicators.note: in signals that these pieces sit inside the tree word

parts.note: the olive is one kind of tree

indicators.note: a coat is the outer layer, so only the outside letters of dull are used

explanation.surface: A drab coat in olive green is described as a help for someone sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' takes the first and last letters of 'dull', DL; with A that makes ADL, which goes 'in' TREE. 'Sewer' is one who sews, not a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot pedal that drives an old sewing machine is a help to a seamstress.

clue.text: Nurses get worried about origin of drugs, but strip

indicators.note: about shows the stirred letters going round the next piece
nurses who get worried are agitated, so the word's letters are stirred up
the origin of a word is its beginning, so the first letter of drugs

explanation.surface: Nurses grow anxious about where some drugs came from, yet take their clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get worried' turns NURSES into UNRESS, which goes 'about' D, the first letter of 'drugs' given by 'origin of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To undress is to take off one's clothes.

clue.text: Diary is empty prior to planning manic driving force

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its first and last letters
planning implies arranging, so the letters of manic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diary stays blank before some frantic planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is empty' leaves DY from 'Diary', and 'planning' turns MANIC into NAMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamic is a force that drives change or progress.

clue.text: The way work on hole is just a temporary measure

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
op is short for opus, a work
a gap is a hole or opening

explanation.surface: Filling a hole in the road is only a short-term fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a makeshift used until something permanent is available.

clue.text: Love a good man (loaded) — a 23!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
ST, for saint, is a good man
loaded is slang for rich

explanation.surface: Fall for a decent wealthy man!
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is ANIMALS: this large flightless bird is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the huge flightless African bird, one creature of the theme.

clue.text: Bush, down under, gets unfashionable support

parts.note: out means out of fashion
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A shrub in Australia receives outdated support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' is the Australian sense: the wild back-country, not a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's remote interior, far from towns, is called the bush.

clue.text: Progress made at home with routes

parts.note: in means at home
roads are routes

explanation.surface: Advances are made close to home along some routes.
explanation.definitionFit: To make inroads is to advance or progress into new territory.

clue.text: Group one firm books a 23

parts.note: a band is a group
I is the Roman numeral for one
CO is short for company, a firm
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A band and one company book a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is ANIMALS: this Australian marsupial is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot is a small long-nosed marsupial of Australia, one creature of the theme.

clue.text: A 23 is astute, but tailless

indicators.note: tailless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: shrewd means astute

explanation.surface: An animal is clever but has no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is ANIMALS: this tiny insect-eating mammal is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrew is a small mouselike insectivore, one creature of the theme.

clue.text: Fleet from 23

definitions.meaning: fleet as an adjective means fast
23 across is ANIMALS, and this fast-flying bird is one of them

explanation.surface: A fleet drawn from the animal kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means quick, and also names a fast-flying bird that is one of the theme's creatures.

clue.text: Charging a couple of thousand during call

indicators.note: during places the thousands inside the calling word

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them

explanation.surface: Someone is charging a couple of grand during a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramming means charging into something with force.

clue.text: Statesman? I'm also a keeper of wildlife!

indicators.note: the words before keep the answer inside them, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A politician claims also to be a zookeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'statesmAN I'M ALSo'; the question mark and exclamation hide the word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals as a group make up the wildlife of a place.

clue.text: People who are economical runners

parts.note: read literally, inexpensive runners such as ice blades; as a whole, stingy people

explanation.surface: Thrifty folk who go jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two: 'cheap' is economical and 'skates' are runners on ice, but the phrase means misers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy people who avoid spending money are called this, a word built from inexpensive ice blades.
